findings.title: Serialized object in cookie 'obj' (PHP serialized object)
findings.owasp: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: A PHP serialized object appears in a user-controllable cookie 'obj'. If deserialized without integrity checks, this can lead to remote code execution via gadget chains.
findings.remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Use data-only formats (JSON) with strict schemas, sign/encrypt serialized state, and use allow-list type filters.

findings.title: Default credentials accepted: admin/admin
findings.nist_csf: PR.AC-1 (Identities & credentials)
findings.description: The login form accepted default credentials 'admin:admin', granting access.
findings.remediation: Force a password change on first login, forbid known default credentials, and add rate limiting / lockout.

findings.title: JWT has no expiration (exp) claim
findings.nist_csf: PR.AC-7 (Authentication)
findings.description: Tokens without expiry remain valid indefinitely if leaked. (token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5...)
findings.remediation: Use a strong random signing key, enforce a fixed allow-list of algorithms (reject 'none'), set short exp lifetimes, and keep sensitive data out of the payload.

findings.remediation: Use a strong random signing key, enforce a fixed allow-list of algorithms (reject 'none'), set short exp lifetimes, and keep sensitive data out of the payload.

findings.title: Client-side prototype pollution
findings.owasp: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: A payload polluted Object.prototype in the browser (Object.prototype.hppc6d18c === 'ad5edf3b'). A vulnerable client-side merge can be abused for DOM XSS, auth bypass, or RCE in gadgets.
findings.remediation: Reject __proto__/constructor/prototype keys when merging untrusted input; use Map or Object.create(null); freeze Object.prototype.

findings.title: CORS misconfiguration: reflects an arbitrary request Origin with credentials allowed

findings.remediation: Validate the Origin against an allow-list of trusted origins; never reflect arbitrary origins, the literal 'null', or combine wildcard ACAO with credentials.

findings.description: The cookie 'token' is missing a security attribute (Cookie set without HttpOnly flag), weakening session protection.
findings.remediation: Set HttpOnly so cookies are inaccessible to JavaScript (mitigates XSS theft).

findings.title: Cookie set without SameSite attribute ('token')
findings.nist_csf: PR.AC-1 (Identities & credentials)
findings.description: The cookie 'token' is missing a security attribute (Cookie set without SameSite attribute), weakening session protection.
findings.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax or Strict to mitigate cross-site request forgery.

findings.title: Server banner disclosed: BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.14.5
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: Example plugin: the Server header advertises 'BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.14.5'.
findings.remediation: Suppress or genericize the Server header.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy header is set, removing a key defense against cross-site scripting and data injection.
findings.remediation: Define a restrictive CSP, e.g. default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'.

findings.title: Missing clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive is set; the page may be framed by an attacker for clickjacking.
findings.remediation: Set X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN) and/or CSP frame-ancestors 'none'.

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: Responses can be MIME-sniffed by browsers, enabling content-type confusion.
findings.remediation: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy header
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: Without a Referrer-Policy, full URLs (possibly containing sensitive data) may leak to third parties via the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Set Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or no-referrer).

findings.title: Version disclosure via Server header
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: The Server header exposes software/version details: 'BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.14.5'.
findings.remediation: Suppress or genericize the Server header to reduce fingerprinting.

findings.title: Mass assignment: server bound unexpected field(s) on POST request
findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
findings.description: The endpoint incorporated attacker-supplied privileged field(s) [account_balance, active, admin, approved, balance, credit, email_verified, enabled, grants, group, group_id, isAdmin, is_active, is_admin, is_staff, is_superuser, is_verified, owner_id, permissions, role, roles, scopes, user_id, verified] into its response object even though they were not part of the documented request. This indicates the request body is bound directly to an internal model (mass assignment / autobinding), allowing a client to set server-controlled properties. Confirm whether the bound values are persisted/honored downstream.
findings.remediation: Bind requests to an explicit allow-list of writable fields (a DTO / serializer with read-only fields marked), never the raw model. Reject or ignore unknown fields and enforce authorization on privileged attributes server-side.

evidence.request_raw: injected fields: account_balance, active, admin, approved, balance, credit, email_verified, enabled, grants, group, group_id, isAdmin, is_active, is_admin, is_staff, is_superuser, is_verified, owner_id, permissions, role, roles, scopes, user_id, verified
evidence.notes: unique nonce for each injected field was reflected in the response (account_balance, active, admin, approved, balance, credit, email_verified, enabled, grants, group, group_id, isAdmin, is_active, is_admin, is_staff, is_superuser, is_verified, owner_id, permissions, role, roles, scopes, user_id, verified)

top_findings.title: OS command injection (output-based) in 'host'
top_findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
top_findings.description: Parameter 'host' is passed to an OS shell; an injected echo command executed and its output was returned. This is remote code execution.
top_findings.remediation: Avoid invoking shells with user input. Use argument arrays / native APIs and strict allow-list validation; never pass user data to a shell string.

evidence.notes: echo canary returned as command output

top_findings.title: Serialized object in cookie 'obj' (PHP serialized object)
top_findings.owasp: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
top_findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
top_findings.description: A PHP serialized object appears in a user-controllable cookie 'obj'. If deserialized without integrity checks, this can lead to remote code execution via gadget chains.
top_findings.remediation: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Use data-only formats (JSON) with strict schemas, sign/encrypt serialized state, and use allow-list type filters.

top_findings.title: SQL injection (error-based, MySQL) in parameter 'id'
top_findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
top_findings.description: Parameter 'id' appears injectable via error-based injection. An attacker may be able to read or modify database contents.
top_findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements; never concatenate user input into SQL. Apply least-privilege DB accounts and input validation.

top_findings.title: Server-side template injection (Jinja2/Twig) in 'name'
top_findings.nist_csf: PR.IP-1 / PR.DS-5 (Secure config / data leak protection)
top_findings.description: Parameter 'name' is evaluated by a server-side template engine (Jinja2/Twig): the expression 1473*2462 returned 3626526. SSTI commonly leads to remote code execution.
top_findings.remediation: Never pass user input into template source. Use logic-less templates or sandboxed rendering and pass user data only as bound variables.

top_findings.title: Default credentials accepted: admin/admin
top_findings.description: The login form accepted default credentials 'admin:admin', granting access.
top_findings.remediation: Force a password change on first login, forbid known default credentials, and add rate limiting / lockout.
